The matrix $A$ has eigenvalues $\lambda_1=2,$ $\lambda_2=1,$ and $\lambda_3=0.$
Find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D=P^{-1}AP.$
question.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.**  Notice that we are already given the eigenvalues of the matrix: 

$\qquad$ $\lambda_1=2,\quad$ $\lambda_2=1, \quad$ $\lambda_3=0.$ 

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ Applying our usual method, we get the following.

- For $\lambda_1=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-2I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives us the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/001911806161a251ef55b16759d586e6d6747a8d34bae00c07eb89c8179cde84.svg)

- For $\lambda_2=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives us the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/413d4dbc71e9f4059fc86d85806e009d5d41dfd8a87b9ea159badcc6003602e5.svg)

- For $\lambda_3=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-0I & =A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-0I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives us the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/187539cd8867c5b8592cf3b6f928992f7be756c25a9a641741ba98150072f307.svg)

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ in the usual way, and this gives us the following:
